definition.text: An absolute extremum is the largest or smallest function value over an interval. A function has an absolute maximum at a point c when its value there is at least as large as every value in the interval, and an absolute minimum at c when its value there is at most as large as every value in the interval.

We say f f has an absolute minimum on I I at c c if f ( c ) ≤ f ( x ) f ( c ) ≤ f ( x ) for all x ∈ I . x ∈ I . If f f has an absolute maximum on I I at c c or an absolute minimum on I I at c , c , we say f f has an absolute extremum on I I at c . c .

definition.text: A test for determining whether a critical point is a local maximum, local minimum, or neither by checking whether the first derivative changes sign around the point.

anchor.quote: This result is known as the first derivative test .

facts.text: If the derivative changes from positive to negative at a critical point, the function has a local maximum there.

anchor.quote: If f ′ f ′ changes sign from positive when x < c x < c to negative when x > c , x > c , then f ( c ) f ( c ) is a local maximum of f . f .

facts.text: If the derivative changes from negative to positive at a critical point, the function has a local minimum there.

anchor.quote: If f ′ f ′ changes sign from negative when x < c x < c to positive when x > c , x > c , then f ( c ) f ( c ) is a local minimum of f . f .

facts.text: If the derivative has the same sign on both sides of a critical point, that point is neither a local maximum nor a local minimum.

anchor.quote: If f ′ f ′ has the same sign for x < c x < c and x > c , x > c , then f ( c ) f ( c ) is neither a local maximum nor a local minimum of f . f .
